hook: Learning a fermionic Gaussian state one copy at a time takes order m^3/eps^2 samples, and no fewer.
summary: For fermionic Gaussian states on m modes, single-copy measurements need and suffice with about m^3/epsilon^2 copies, versus m^2/epsilon^2 for collective measurements. The authors also fill in many entries of the sample-complexity table for bosonic and block-measurement cases. These are theoretical bounds, and the lower bound holds only for small epsilon.
title: Sample complexity of learning fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states with single-copy and entangled measurements
